brief: Desk note combining a market recap, a GIR rates call, and single-name updates. Industrials closed down 125bps and materials down 80bps yesterday, underperforming broader markets. Both are down sharply for the month, 465bps and 750bps. Futures are firmer this morning, lifted by Micron's bullish forecast, while Europe lags on France's budget reveal and Brent holds above $100. GIR's causal chain: August core PCE rose 0.25% m/m and 3.01% y/y, both below expectations, partly from a methodology-driven revision. This leads GS to forecast 3.0% Q4/Q4 core PCE versus the FOMC median of 3.4%, which combined with NY Fed President Williams' comments leads GS to see an October hike as unlikely, pushing the second hike to December with a strong chance the FOMC ultimately hikes no further. Separately, Q2 GDP was revised up 0.7pp to +2.2% and 2026Q1 up 0.4pp to +2.5%, while Q3 GDP tracking was trimmed 0.1pp to +3.3% on weaker Advance Economic Indicators data. The note also reports an AYI fiscal Q4 beat, a constructive PWR update reiterating Buy, and an AAL/LUV field trip citing resilient demand despite higher fuel.
